title: Density Gradient Multilayered Polymerization (DGMP): A Novel Technique for Creating Multi-compartment, Customizable Scaffolds for Tissue Engineering
protocol: React the RGDS peptide with acryloyl-PEG-succinimidyl carboxymethyl ester (aPEG-SCM) and N,N-diisopropylethylamine (DIPEA) at a molar ratio of 1.2:1:2 in DMSO under argon at room temperature overnight.
Confirm conjugation by matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time of flight (MALDI-TOF) mass spectrometry.
Add 1 μl of the aPEG-RGDS reaction solution to a sample spot on the MALDI target and dry.
Prepare a saturated solution of Universal MALDI Matrix in tetrahydrofuran (THF) and vortex for 1 min.
Add approximately 1 μl of the prepared matrix solution to the same sample spot as the aPEG-RGDS solution.
Repeat the procedure for aPEG-SCM for comparison.
Load and analyze the samples using MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry.

To conjugate the fluorophore, add an equimolar amount of Alexa Fluor 350 carboxylic acid (succinimidyl ester), dissolved in DMSO, to the aPEG-RGDS reaction solution and react under argon at room temperature overnight.
Purify aPEG-RGDS-350 by dialyzing against DI-H2O at 4 °C for 48 hours with a MWCO of 3500 Da at a volumetric ratio of 1,000:1, exchanging the dialysate at least twice per day.
Freeze dry the purified aPEG-RGDS-350 using a Labconco Freezone Plus or equivalent freeze drying system and store at -20 °C.
Prepare hydrophobic glass slides by placing clean glass slides into a glass dish.
Heat the glass dish with slides to 80 °C for 30 min.
Add 250 μl Sigmacote to each slide and gently rock for 30 sec to coat entirely.
Rinse coated slides thoroughly with 100% methanol followed by washing in distilled water.
Soak the washed slides twice for 5 min in at least 10 ml of solution.
Cut silicone spacers using 10 mm biopsy punches.
Autoclave the silicone spacers and Sigmacote-treated glass slides.
Mix PEG diacrylate (PEGda) precursor to a final concentration of 15% w/v with varying amounts of iodixanol in PBS for different densities.
Add photoinitiator (2-Hydroxy-4'-(2-hydroxyethoxy)-2-methylpropiophenone, 10 μl stock solution per ml) last to prevent premature polymerization.
Repeat the mixing process for aPEG-RGDS-350 with varying iodixanol concentrations in PBS and photoinitiator addition.
Filter-sterilize each solution using a sterile 1 ml syringe and 0.2 μm filter.
Sandwich the spacer between two Sigmacore-treated glass slides.
Secure the setup with clamps as depicted.
Add the most dense solution first to cast layered gels.
Follow by adding a less dense solution.
Repeat alternate layering to achieve desired composition and densities.
Irradiate the mold with 365 nm light for 3 min using a portable UVR-9000 lamp.
Allow the polymerized gels to cure for 5 min.
Remove the clamps gently.
Lift the top glass slide and the mold carefully.
Place the stratified DGMP gels in a 50 ml tube containing sterile PBS or culture medium for washing.
Wash the polymerized gels in PBS at a 1,000:1 volumetric ratio.
Exchange buffer at least twice per day to remove density modifier, photoinitiator, and unreacted polymer.
Alternatively, exchange PBS with cell growth medium.
Store the DGMP gels in PBS or growth medium for future use.
Arrange DGMP gel along a ruler on the sample tray of a VersaDoc gel documentation unit.
Expose the gels in 350 nm; exposure time varies depending on fluorophore concentration.
Gently insert DGMP gels into the wells of 48-well cell culture plates using a sterile cell scraper.
Pre-warm growth medium and PBS in a water bath set at 37 °C.
Wash a 60% confluent plate of C2C12 cells three times with PBS.
Aspirate off PBS.
Add 1 ml of 0.25% Trypsin-EDTA to the cells and incubate at 37 °C for 2 min.
Resuspend the cells in growth medium and count cells.
Seed the DGMP gel-containing well with C2C12 myoblasts (20,000 cells/cm²).
Incubate the cells at 37 °C in 5% CO₂/95% relative humidity.
Gently exchange medium after 4 hr; be careful not to remove lightly adhered cells.
After 24 hours, confirm the attachment of C2C12 myoblasts on RGDS-containing layers of DGMP gels by epifluorescence and phase contrast microscopy.
